motivation: Durable colony-code losses are strongly concentrated among small groups under an exchangeable null, but that size ordering is fully compatible with neutral size-dependent demographic thinning. A mechanistic test therefore needs an independent biological performance endpoint measured before disappearance.

external_dataset.title: Adelie penguin colony-specific chick production, 1991, present.
external_dataset.season_alignment: For January chick censuses, season_start_year = calendar year(time) - 1 and is matched to the November adult breeding census of that year.

question: Do Palmer Adelie colony codes that undergo durable extinction in the following census already show depressed reproductive success in the immediately preceding breeding season?

population_frame.risk_sets: Use the primary durable-extinction risk sets from PALMER_COLONY_EXTINCTION_HAZARD_V1, indexed by island and adult census year t, with event status defined at t+1.
population_frame.match: Exact match on island, raw colony_code string and season_start_year=t.
population_frame.eligibility: Require finite nonnegative num_chicks, finite num_breeding_pairs > 0 in the chick dataset, and a classified event/non-event transition at t -> t+1.

response.primary: chicks_per_pair = num_chicks / num_breeding_pairs from the January chick-production census.
response.risk_set_standardization: Within each matched island-year risk set, z-standardize chicks_per_pair when at least 3 matched colonies are present and SD > 0.
response.primary_contrast: Mean z(chicks_per_pair) among next-year durable-extinction colonies minus mean among next-year non-events, averaged with equal weight across informative event-bearing risk sets.

primary_inference.null: Within each informative matched island-year risk set, next-year event labels are exchangeable with respect to the already-observed chick-success values.
primary_inference.permutation: Preserve the observed number of events in each risk set and permute event identities among matched colonies.
primary_inference.p_value: one-sided lower-tail Monte Carlo p with +1 correction

size_success_gradient.question: Do smaller contemporaneous breeding groups have lower chick success within the same island-year?
size_success_gradient.predictor: within-risk-set z(log1p adult breeding pairs) from the adult census at t
size_success_gradient.statistic: pooled OLS slope after island-year demeaning, equivalent to a within-risk-set association
size_success_gradient.permutation: shuffle chick-success values within island-year risk sets; 100000 draws; seed 20260941

event_effect_after_size.question: Do next-year extinction colonies underperform even after accounting for current group size?
event_effect_after_size.model: z(chicks_per_pair) ~ event_next_year + z(log1p current pairs) + island indicators + centered year
event_effect_after_size.role: descriptive effect-size decomposition; primary permutation remains the confirmatory gate

survivor_island_trajectory.question: As breeding distributions concentrate, is island-level reproductive output per breeding pair maintained, improved or degraded?
survivor_island_trajectory.metric: total chicks / total chick-dataset breeding pairs across matched positive colonies within each island-season
survivor_island_trajectory.concentration_predictor: effective colony number from the adult census in the same season
survivor_island_trajectory.role: descriptive mechanism discrimination only; not a causal test

sensitivities.log1p_success: Repeat the primary risk-set contrast using z(log1p(chicks_per_pair)).
sensitivities.rank_success: Repeat using within-risk-set fractional ranks of chicks_per_pair.
sensitivities.exclude_litchfield: Repeat primary analysis after excluding Litchfield.
sensitivities.prior_count_ge2: Repeat after requiring adult prior count >= 2 pairs.
sensitivities.denominator_overlap: Report exact equality fraction between chick-dataset num_breeding_pairs and the November adult census denominator for the matched island-colony-season rows.

decision_logic.preextinction_reproductive_failure_suppo: Primary contrast < 0 and one-sided permutation p <= 0.05.
decision_logic.social_facilitation_consistent: Secondary size-success gradient > 0 with permutation p <= 0.05.
decision_logic.good_site_retreat_pattern: Primary pre-extinction failure is absent while island-level chicks per pair is maintained or increases as effective colony number declines.
decision_logic.broad_local_failure_pattern: Primary pre-extinction failure is present and/or island-level chicks per pair declines as concentration increases.
decision_logic.no_mechanistic_resolution: If neither pre-extinction reproductive failure nor size-success gradient is supported, retain concentration as demographic reorganization without assigning a social or reproductive mechanism.

interpretation_boundaries: Chick success can support temporal ordering of reproductive performance before disappearance but does not by itself identify predation, snow or social facilitation.
The chick numerator is a distinct life-stage endpoint; the breeding-pair denominator may overlap the adult census and must be audited.
Do not change the event definition, season alignment, response, risk-set weighting or primary permutation after chick outcomes are opened.
Do not treat a null result as evidence that all surviving breeding sites are equal in quality.
